gloss: be glad, rejoice; make glad; joy, gladness, festivity
summary: שָׂמַח is to be glad: the gladness of heart at a sight or news, at a son who is wise, at Yahweh's salvation, and above all the gladness Israel was commanded to have before Yahweh at his feasts and offerings, as at the feast of booths, “and you shall rejoice before Yahweh your God seven days” (Lev 23:40). The piel makes glad (wine, a good word, a wise son, Yahweh's deeds), and שִׂמְחָה is both the joy itself and the festive rejoicing that shows it, “the day of your gladness” on which the trumpets sound (Num 10:10). The same gladness can be turned wrong, in mirth that ignores death and judgment or in gloating over another's fall, and scripture judges both. Ugaritic has the same verb šmḫ “rejoice” and noun šmḫt “joy”, with ḫ behind ח.

words.gloss: be glad, rejoice; (piel, hiphil) make glad

senses.gloss: be glad (at what one sees or hears)
senses.definition: To be glad in heart at something seen, heard or received: a brother coming, the ark returning, news of deliverance, a wise son. Its opposite is grief or groaning.

evidence.note: Aaron “will see you and be glad (וְשָׂמַח) in his heart”.
Beth-shemesh lifted their eyes, saw the ark, “and rejoiced to see it”.
Told that deliverance would come tomorrow, the men of Jabesh “were glad”.
The girl's father saw the Levite “and was glad to meet him”.
Hiram heard Solomon's words and “was glad exceedingly”, blessing Yahweh.
Hezekiah “was glad of them” and showed the envoys his treasure.
Jonah rejoiced over the plant “a great gladness”.
All the people of the land rejoiced and the city was quiet.
Sailors “are glad because they are quiet”.
Egypt “was glad when they went out”.
“My son, if your heart is wise, my heart will be glad, even mine.”
Beside גִּיל: the father of a righteous man exults; he who begets a wise son is glad in him.
Set against תּוּגָה: he who begets a fool has grief, and the father of a fool “is not glad”.
When the righteous increase the people are glad; when the wicked rule the people groan.
“If I was glad because my wealth was great”.

senses.gloss: rejoice before Yahweh (at feast and sacrifice)
senses.definition: To rejoice in Yahweh's presence at the place he chooses, eating the offerings and the produce he has given, with the whole household, the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless and the widow: a gladness the law commands.

evidence.note: At the feast of booths: take fruit and branches “and rejoice before Yahweh your God seven days”.
At the feast of weeks: “you shall rejoice before Yahweh your God”, you, your son and daughter, servants, the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless and the widow.
“And you shall rejoice in your feast”, at booths.
“You shall eat there before Yahweh your God and rejoice in all you put your hand to.”
The tithe turned to money and spent at the place: “eat there before Yahweh your God and rejoice, you and your household”.
With the firstfruits: “rejoice in all the good Yahweh your God has given you”.
On Ebal: “sacrifice peace offerings, eat there, and rejoice before Yahweh your God”.
Peace offerings before Yahweh at Gilgal, and Saul and all Israel “rejoiced greatly”.
“They rejoice before you as with the gladness of harvest.”
The people rejoiced that they had offered willingly, with a whole heart.
Judah rejoiced at the oath, for they had sworn with all their heart.
At Hezekiah's Passover all the assembly rejoiced, with the strangers.
At the dedication of the wall: “they rejoiced, for God had made them rejoice with great gladness”.

senses.gloss: rejoice in Yahweh, his salvation, his word
senses.definition: To be glad with Yahweh himself, his salvation, his kindness or his word as the cause, said by the righteous, the humble and those who seek him.

evidence.note: Hannah: “my heart exults in Yahweh… for I rejoice in your salvation”.
“Rejoice in Yahweh and exult, righteous ones.”
“I will rejoice in Yahweh.”
“I will be glad and exult in you.”
“Therefore my heart is glad and my glory rejoices; my flesh also shall dwell in safety”, quoted at Act 2:26.
“For in him our heart is glad, because we have trusted in his holy name.”
“Let the heart of those who seek Yahweh rejoice.”
“I will exult and be glad in your kindness.”
He turned the sea to dry land: “there we rejoiced in him”.
“This is the day Yahweh has made; let us exult and rejoice in it.”
Those who fear Yahweh see the psalmist and are glad, “because I have hoped in your word”.
“I was glad when they said to me, Let us go to the house of Yahweh.”
“Let Israel rejoice in his maker.”
“This is Yahweh; we have waited for him; let us exult and rejoice in his salvation.”
“My servants shall rejoice, and you shall be ashamed.”
When Yahweh turns back the captivity of his people, Israel shall be glad.
“Will you not revive us again, that your people may rejoice in you?”
“Sons of Zion, exult and rejoice in Yahweh your God.”
“Sing and rejoice, daughter of Zion, for behold, I come and I will dwell in your midst.”
Their heart shall be glad as with wine; their heart shall exult in Yahweh.
Those who despised the day of small things shall rejoice and see the plummet in Zerubbabel's hand.
The righteous see the end of the wicked and are glad.

senses.gloss: (heavens, earth, nations) rejoice at Yahweh's reign
senses.definition: The heavens, the earth, the coastlands and the nations called to be glad because Yahweh reigns and comes to judge.

evidence.note: “Let the heavens rejoice and the earth exult… before Yahweh, for he comes to judge the earth” (v. 13).
“Yahweh reigns; let the earth exult, let the many coastlands rejoice.”
“And let them say among the nations, Yahweh reigns.”
“Let the peoples rejoice and sing, for you judge the peoples uprightly.”
Mount Zion rejoices because of his judgments.

senses.definition: Yahweh himself rejoicing in his works, or refusing to rejoice over a godless people.

evidence.note: “Let the glory of Yahweh be for ever; let Yahweh rejoice in his works.”
“Therefore the Lord will not rejoice over their young men”, for every one is godless.

senses.definition: With ל or עַל or at a calamity: to be glad at another's ruin, an enemy's stumbling or a neighbour's desolation, often beside “magnify oneself against”; scripture forbids it and judges it.

evidence.note: “When your enemy falls, do not rejoice, and when he stumbles let not your heart exult.”
“Do not rejoice over me, my enemy: when I fall, I shall arise.”
Edom should not have rejoiced over the sons of Judah in the day of their destruction.
“At my stumbling they rejoiced and gathered together.”
“Lest they rejoice over me; when my foot slips they magnify themselves (הִגְדִּילוּ) against me.”
“If I rejoiced at the ruin of him who hated me”, among Job's oath of innocence.
Ammon clapped its hands and rejoiced with all the despite of its soul against the land of Israel.
“Tell it not in Gath… lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice.”
“Do not rejoice, all Philistia, because the rod that struck you is broken.”
The cypresses rejoice over the fallen king of Babylon: “no feller comes up against us”.
“Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Edom”, in irony: the cup will pass to you too.
The Chaldean draws men up in his net, “therefore he rejoices and exults”.

senses.gloss: enjoy, take pleasure in (life, youth, a wife, one's work)
senses.definition: To be glad in the goods of life under the sun: food and drink, one's labour, the wife of one's youth, youth itself, held as God's gift and under his judgment.

evidence.note: “There is nothing better for them than to rejoice and to do good in their life.”
To eat, take one's portion and rejoice in one's labour, “this is the gift of God”.
Nothing better under the sun “than to eat and to drink and to be glad”.
“Rejoice, young man, in your youth… but know that for all these God will bring you into judgment.”
“Let your fountain be blessed, and rejoice in the wife of your youth.”
“We will exult and rejoice in you.”
“Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out.”
The wicked “rejoice at the sound of the pipe”.
Set against mourning: in the day of wrath “let not the buyer rejoice nor the seller mourn”.
“Do not rejoice, Israel, unto exultation like the peoples, for you have gone whoring from your God.”

senses.definition: Once, of a light: the light of the righteous “rejoices”, set against the lamp of the wicked going out, so burns bright.

evidence.note: “The light of the righteous rejoices (יִשְׂמָח), but the lamp of the wicked goes out.”

senses.definition: To cause someone to be glad: a son his father, a man his new wife, wine and oil the heart, a good word an anxious heart.

evidence.note: “A wise son makes a father glad, but a foolish son is the grief of his mother.”
“Be wise, my son, and make my heart glad.”
A newly married man is free for his house a year “and shall make glad his wife whom he has taken”.
“Wine makes glad the heart of man.”
The vine's new wine “makes glad God and men”.
“Wine makes life glad.”
Anxiety in the heart weighs it down, but a good word makes it glad.
Oil and incense make the heart glad.
Stringed instruments from ivory palaces make the king glad.
The man who brought word “A son is born to you”, “making him very glad”.
“With their wickedness they make the king glad.”

senses.definition: Yahweh gladdening his servants by his deeds, his precepts, his deliverance, and in his house.

evidence.note: “For you, Yahweh, have made me glad by your work.”
“I will turn their mourning into joy, comfort them, and make them rejoice from their sorrow.”
“Make us glad according to the days you afflicted us.”
“Make glad the soul of your servant.”
“The precepts of Yahweh are right, making glad the heart.”
A river whose streams make glad the city of God.
The foreigners: “I will make them joyful in my house of prayer.”
They kept the feast of unleavened bread with joy, “for Yahweh had made them joyful”.

senses.definition: To give an enemy cause to gloat over someone, said of Yahweh when he gives his people up, or denied when he delivers them.

evidence.note: “You have drawn me up and have not made my enemies rejoice over me.”
Yahweh “has made the enemy rejoice over you”.

senses.definition: Once, as the piel: to give enemies cause to rejoice.

evidence.note: Of David's line cast off: “you have made all his enemies rejoice”.

greek.gloss: make glad; (passive) be glad, make merry

“It was right to make merry (εὐφρανθῆναι) and be glad.”
The rich man: “eat, drink, εὐφραίνου”, as Ecc 8:15.
“Therefore εὐφραίνεσθε, heavens”, as Psa 96:11.

“χαίρετε in the Lord always.”
Love οὐ χαίρει at unrighteousness, against gloating (Pro 24:17).

opposites.note: Be ashamed: Yahweh's servants rejoice, his enemies are ashamed.

phrases.gloss: rejoice a great gladness, rejoice exceedingly

senses.definition: The gladness felt in the heart: given by God, found in his word and presence, belonging to the righteous; the opposite of grief and mourning.

evidence.note: “You have put שִׂמְחָה in my heart, more than when their grain and new wine abound.”
“Your words were to me a joy and the gladness of my heart.”
“Even in laughter the heart aches, and the end of שִׂמְחָה is grief (תּוּגָה).”
“The heart knows its own bitterness, and a stranger does not share its gladness.”
“You have turned my mourning into dancing; you have loosed my sackcloth and girded me with gladness.”
“Make me hear joy and gladness.”
“Fulness of gladnesses (שְׂמָחוֹת) is with your face”, quoted at Act 2:28.
“You make him glad with gladness with your face.”
“To God, the gladness of my exultation.”
“Light is sown for the righteous, and gladness for the upright in heart.”
“The hope of the righteous is gladness.”
“A man has joy in the answer of his mouth.”
“It is joy to the righteous to do judgment.”
“The humble shall increase their gladness in Yahweh.”
To the man who is good before him God gives wisdom, knowledge and gladness.
“God answers him in the gladness of his heart.”
Solomon's wedding day, “the day of the gladness of his heart”.
“If I do not set Jerusalem above my chief joy.”
Of Yahweh: “he will rejoice over you with gladness (בְּשִׂמְחָה)”.

senses.definition: Gladness shown outwardly: the celebration with song, music, feasting and offerings, at the feasts, at bringing up the ark, at a king's anointing, at a dedication; also a day kept for it.

evidence.note: “In the day of your gladness, and in your appointed feasts and the beginnings of your months, you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings.”
The fourteenth of Adar made “a day of feasting and gladness”.
“The month turned for them from sorrow to gladness and from mourning to a good day.”
Laban: “I would have sent you away with gladness and songs, with tambourine and lyre.”
David brought up the ark from Obed-edom's house “with gladness”.
Singers with lyres, harps and cymbals, raising the sound “for gladness”.
At Solomon's anointing the people piped and rejoiced “a great gladness”.
They ate and drank before Yahweh “with great gladness”.
Burnt offerings “with gladness and with song”, as David appointed.
Hezekiah's feast of unleavened bread seven days “with great gladness”.
They kept another seven days “of gladness”.
At the founding of the second house, shouting for joy beside the old men's weeping.
The people went to eat and drink, send portions “and make great gladness, because they had understood the words”.
Keeping the booths as not since Joshua, “there was very great gladness”.
“Gladness of heart, as when one goes with the pipe to come into the mountain of Yahweh.”
“As the gladness in harvest.”
The king's bride brought in “with gladness and exultation”.
“Serve Yahweh with gladness; come before him with singing.”
The curse falls “because you did not serve Yahweh your God with gladness and goodness of heart for the abundance of all things”.
The fasts of the fourth, fifth, seventh and tenth months shall become “joy and gladness and good appointed feasts”.
The Philistine lords gathered to sacrifice to Dagon “and for rejoicing”.
Captors asked for “gladness”, a song of Zion.
Gladness taken from Moab's fruitful field, no treading in the presses.
“All gladness is darkened; the joy of the land is gone.”
Food cut off, “gladness and exultation from the house of our God”.
“The voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride” made to cease.
The same voices heard again, with those bringing thanksgiving to Yahweh's house.

senses.definition: Merriment pursued for its own sake, weighed and found empty, or kept up in the face of judgment and death.

evidence.note: “I will test you with שִׂמְחָה… and behold, this also was vapour.”
“Of laughter I said, It is mad; and of שִׂמְחָה, What does it do?”
Against the house of mourning: “the heart of fools is in the house of שִׂמְחָה”.
“He who loves שִׂמְחָה will be a poor man; he who loves wine and oil will not be rich.”
“Folly is joy to him who lacks heart.”
When Yahweh called to weeping: “behold, joy and gladness, slaying oxen… let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die”; quoted at 1Co 15:32.
“The joy of the godless is but for a moment.”
Yet the Preacher commends שִׂמְחָה with eating and drinking as what God gives under the sun.

senses.definition: Gladness at another's desolation, the joy Edom took in Israel's ruin.

evidence.note: “As you rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel because it was desolate, so will I do to you.”
Edom took Yahweh's land “with the joy of all their heart, with despite of soul”.

senses.gloss: the everlasting joy of the redeemed
senses.definition: The gladness Yahweh promises to the ransomed returning to Zion, which sorrow will not overtake.

evidence.note: “The ransomed of Yahweh shall return and come to Zion with singing, and everlasting joy upon their heads; they shall obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.”
Zion's desert made like Eden: “joy and gladness shall be found in her”.
“Everlasting joy shall be theirs.”
“You shall go out with joy.”
Those cast out for his name's sake: “he shall appear to your joy”.
“To rejoice in the gladness of your nation.”

evidence.locator: שִׂמְחָה → εὐφροσύνη ×57 (lemma count, MACULA alignment); Num.10.10, Psa.16.11, Ecc.8.15, Zep.3.17

evidence.note: Peter quotes Psa 16:11: “you will make me full of εὐφροσύνης with your face”.
God “filling our hearts with food and εὐφροσύνης”, as Psa 4:8.

evidence.locator: שִׂמְחָה → χαρά ×6 (lemma count, MACULA alignment); Jon.4.6, Jer.15.16, Psa.21.7, Pro.14.13

evidence.note: “They rejoiced with exceeding great χαράν”, as Jonah “rejoiced a great gladness” (Jon 4:6).
The friend of the bridegroom rejoices at the bridegroom's voice: “this my χαρά is fulfilled”.
“For the χαρᾶς set before him” Jesus endured the cross.

parallels.note: Feasting, in “a day of feasting and gladness”.

opposites.note: Sorrow, which flees from the everlasting joy.
Mourning: the house of mourning against the house of mirth.

words.summary: The verbal adjective: glad, of a heart, a people at a feast or a coronation, a mother of children; and, as a noun, those who are glad at another's evil.

senses.definition: In a state of gladness: of a people eating and drinking in peace, going home from the feast, of a heart that makes the face good.

evidence.note: After the seven days of booths: “and you shall be altogether glad (אַךְ שָׂמֵחַ)”.
Judah and Israel “eating and drinking and glad”.
After the dedication they went to their tents “glad and good of heart”.
“A glad heart makes the face good, but by sorrow of heart the spirit is broken.”
“A glad heart does good like a medicine.”
The barren woman made “a glad mother of children”.
“Yahweh has done great things for us; we are glad.”
They came up from Gihon rejoicing at Solomon's anointing.
All the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets at Joash's crowning.
“All the glad of heart sigh” when the new wine mourns.
Haman went out “glad and good of heart”.
Those who “are glad unto exultation” when they find the grave.

senses.definition: As a noun, those glad at another's calamity or at doing evil.

evidence.note: “He who is glad at calamity will not go unpunished.”
“Those glad at my evil”, beside “those who magnify themselves against me”.
“Who are glad to do evil.”
“You who rejoice in a thing of nought”, boasting of their own strength.
“Rejoice with those who rejoice (χαιρόντων).”

cognates.note: Segert's glossary gives the verb /š-m-ḫ/ with the forms tšmḫ, yšmḫ, nšmḫ “to rejoice”, beside Hebrew śāmē(a)ḥ, yiśmaḥ; in the letter 2.16 the jussive tšmḫ “may (my) mother rejoice”, which he compares with Prov 5:18. Ugaritic writes ḫ and ḥ with different signs, so ḫ stands behind ח; Ugaritic š also stands for older ś (Hebrew שׂ).

evidence.note: “/š-m-ḫ/: tšmḫ, yšmḫ, nšmḫ “to rejoice” (H. śāmē(a)ḥ, yiśmaḥ)”. Page image read (leaf n229).
“/tišmaḫ/ jussive 3. sing. f. /š-m-ḫ/ “to rejoice”… cf. H. Prov 5:18”.

cognates.note: The noun answers to שִׂמְחָה in form and sense, and to its use with the heart: ymlu lbh šmḫt “her heart was filled with joy” (KTU 1.3:II:25–26), as Hebrew “the gladness of my heart” (Jer 15:16).

evidence.note: “her heart was filled with joy”. Page image read (leaf n125).

cognates.gloss: be high, lofty; (with the nose) magnify oneself, be proud
cognates.note: Arabic š and ḫ answer regularly to Hebrew שׂ and to the ḫ Ugaritic shows behind ח, so the sounds match. Lane gives “it (a mountain) was high, or lofty”, and of a man “he magnified, or exalted, himself; was proud”, raising his nose. The meaning is not “rejoice”, but it meets the Hebrew where gladness over another's fall is set beside “magnify oneself against” (Psa 35:26; 38:17) and in exultant boasting (Amo 6:13). Recorded as possible: no Arabic sense of joy is attested for the root.

evidence.note: a lofty mountain; proud, raising the nose

cognates.gloss: flourish, grow luxuriantly; (adj. šamḫu) luxuriant, magnificent
cognates.note: Akkadian š and ḫ match the Ugaritic šmḫ. The sense is of growth and splendour, not of joy; it may meet the Hebrew in Pro 13:9, where the light of the righteous “rejoices”, that is shines out, against a lamp going out. Recorded as possible.

luxuriant, magnificent, prosperous

doctrine.statement: At the feast of booths Israel takes fruit and branches “and you shall rejoice before Yahweh your God seven days” (Lev 23:40), and Deuteronomy commands the same gladness at the place he chooses, for son and daughter, servants, the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless and the widow together, “and you shall be altogether glad” (Deu 16:11, 14–15), eating the offerings and peace offerings before him (Deu 12:7, 12; 27:7). The trumpets are blown over the offerings “in the day of your gladness and in your appointed feasts” (Num 10:10). The curse comes “because you did not serve Yahweh your God with gladness and goodness of heart for the abundance of all things” (Deu 28:47), and the psalm calls, “Serve Yahweh with gladness” (Psa 100:2). When the returned exiles understood the law read to them, they made great gladness and kept the booths with “very great gladness” (Neh 8:12, 17). Paul writes, “Rejoice in the Lord always” (Php 4:4). From the verses: gladness before Yahweh is part of what he commands in worship, grounded in what he has given and shared with the poor and the stranger; to have plenty from him and not be glad in him is counted against his people.

David says, “Therefore my heart is glad and my glory rejoices; my flesh also shall dwell in safety, for you will not leave my soul to the grave, nor give your holy one to see corruption; you will make known to me the path of life; fulness of gladnesses is with your face” (Psa 16:9–11). Peter quotes these words, “my heart was glad… you will make me full of gladness with your face”, and says that David, being a prophet, “spoke of the resurrection of the Christ, that his soul was not left in the grave, neither did his flesh see corruption” (Act 2:25–31). Hebrews says Jesus “for the joy set before him endured the cross” and sat down at the right hand of God (Heb 12:2). From the verses: the gladness of Psalm 16 is a gladness of the flesh in hope, resting on not being left in the grave; the fulness of joy is reached by resurrection to the path of life in God's presence, first in Christ.

The Preacher commends gladness in eating, drinking and one's labour as the gift of God (Ecc 3:12–13; 5:18; 8:15; 9:7), yet tested mirth for its own sake and found it vapour, “of gladness, what does it do?” (Ecc 2:1–2), and binds the young man's gladness to judgment: “Rejoice, young man, in your youth… but know that for all these God will bring you into judgment” (Ecc 11:9). When Yahweh called Jerusalem to weeping and sackcloth, there was instead “joy and gladness, slaying oxen… let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die”, and Yahweh answered that this iniquity would not be covered until they died (Isa 22:12–14). Paul takes up those words: if the dead are not raised, “let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die” (1Co 15:32). Jesus' rich man tells his soul to eat, drink and be merry, and God answers, “Fool, this night your soul is required of you” (Luk 12:19–20). From the verses: gladness in God's gifts is right when it is held under his judgment; mirth that takes death as the end is the answer of those without hope of resurrection, and scripture counts it iniquity.

“When your enemy falls, do not rejoice… lest Yahweh see it and it be evil in his eyes” (Pro 24:17–18); “he who is glad at calamity will not go unpunished” (Pro 17:5). Job counts gladness at the ruin of one who hated him among the sins he swears he did not commit (Job 31:29–30). Edom should not have rejoiced over Judah in the day of their destruction (Oba 1:12), and Yahweh answers it in kind: “as you rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel because it was desolate, so will I do to you” (Ezk 35:15; 25:6–7). Yet the righteous rejoice when Yahweh's judgment is done (Psa 58:11), and “it is joy to the righteous to do judgment” (Pro 21:15). Paul writes that love “does not rejoice at unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth” (1Co 13:6). From the verses: what is condemned is gladness at a man's ruin for its own sake; gladness that Yahweh's righteousness is done is not condemned, and he repays the first measure for measure.

Jeremiah says Yahweh will make to cease from Judah “the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride”, for the land shall be desolate (Jer 7:34; 16:9; 25:10), and then that those same voices will be heard again in Jerusalem's streets with those who bring thanksgiving into Yahweh's house, when he turns back the captivity of the land (Jer 33:10–11). John the Baptist calls himself the friend of the bridegroom, who “rejoices greatly because of the bridegroom's voice: this my joy is fulfilled” (Jhn 3:29). Of Babylon the great it is said that “the voice of bridegroom and bride shall be heard in you no more” (Rev 18:23). From the verses: the gladness of the wedding marks a people under Yahweh's favour and its silence his judgment; John hears its return in the voice of Jesus as the bridegroom.

The psalms call the heavens to rejoice and the earth to exult “before Yahweh, for he comes, for he comes to judge the earth” (Psa 96:11–13), “Yahweh reigns; let the earth exult, let the many coastlands rejoice” (Psa 97:1; 1Ch 16:31), and the peoples to rejoice “for you judge the peoples uprightly” (Psa 67:5). Zechariah tells the daughter of Zion to sing and rejoice, “for behold, I come and I will dwell in your midst”, and many nations shall join themselves to Yahweh in that day (Zec 2:14–15); Zephaniah adds that Yahweh in her midst “will rejoice over you with gladness” (Zep 3:14–17). Isaiah's people say in that day, “This is Yahweh; we have waited for him; let us exult and rejoice in his salvation” (Isa 25:9). In Revelation the great multitude says, “Let us rejoice and exult… for the marriage of the Lamb has come” (Rev 19:6–7). From the verses: the gladness of the whole earth is tied to Yahweh's coming to reign and judge from Zion, a gladness he shares over his people, and it is still looked for at Christ's return.
